title: client_ip trusts the first X-Forwarded-For hop, which is client-spoofable even behind Cloudflare; the code comment and new migration trust note assert the opposite
detail: Cloudflare appends the true connecting IP to the END of any client-supplied XFF header, preserving attacker-controlled leading entries, so the captured first hop is forgeable via Cloudflare too. The comment/trust note codify a wrong assumption; the captured IP becomes fabricated evidence feeding RC3.7 fraud comparators.
recommended_fix: Read CF-Connecting-IP (or the last XFF entry) in client_ip; correct the comment and migration trust note to state the first XFF hop is client-controlled.

(diff, deferred-work.md) summary: request_helpers.client_ip/client_user_agent slice by graphemes (Gleam string.slice) while the DB CHECK bounds count characters (Postgres length()) — a multi-codepoint header can exceed the bound post-slice and 500 the write path.
detail: Gleam string.slice counts graphemes; Postgres length() counts codepoints. A header of 64 multi-codepoint grapheme clusters stays 64 graphemes post-slice but exceeds 64 codepoints, violating the CHECK and aborting the submission. Contradicts the spec matrix's 'CHECK constraints never trip'; already deferred.
recommended_fix: Truncate by codepoints (matching Postgres length()) before write in request_helpers, applied across cookie_consent_log, payment_terms_acceptance, and application capture callers.
